titel: Martin V to Cardinal Branda: the crusade bull of 1421
quelle: František Palacký, Urkundliche Beiträge zur Geschichte des Hussitenkrieges vom Jahre 1419 an, vol. I (Prague: Tempsky, 1873), no. 74, pp. 70–75, after Andreas of Regensburg's Supplementa, ff. 385–386 (internet archive: urkundlichebeit01palagoog). English: the site's working translation.
hinweis: Dated Rome, St Peter's, 13 April 1421 (the Ides of April, in the fourth year of the pontificate). Martin V appoints Cardinal Branda da Castiglione his legate for Bohemia, Moravia and Meissen and gives him power to preach the crusade and grant its indulgences. Palacký prints the bull from the collection of Andreas of Regensburg, who copied the documents of the campaign. The excerpts follow Palacký's text with his spelling, including the ae ligature; omissions are marked [...]. Palacký notes one manuscript reading on p. 72.

sections.blurb: The charge against the Hussites, the legate's mission, the call to every estate, the preaching of the cross, the indulgences graded by person, purse and prayer, and the absolution of crusaders even for arson and sacrilege.

units.titel: The charge: they burn churches and images
units.orig: Considerantes igitur iniquitatis alumpnos Wiklefistas et Hussistas aliosque hereticos et infideles, qui vere salutis semitam deserentes, christiane religionis persecutores acerrimos sese reddunt, quique falsis et insanis dogmatibus ac dampnatis erroribus heresumque fomentis orthodoxam fidem euertere molientes, vniuersum regnum Bohemie et partes illi conterminas infecerunt, ac cupientes illorum temeritati quantum cum deo possumus obuiare, fideles milites Christi pugiles, athletas viuifice crucis, qua nos a dampnacione redemit, caractere insignitos contra præfatos hereticos duximus excitandos, ut hereticos ipsos, qui eciam dei timore postposito ecclesias, monasteria, et alia pia loca in honorem Christi virginisque gloriose, apostolorum, martyrum et confessorum dedicata, eorumque ymagines concremant et euertunt, et fidem catholicam præsertim in nacione Germanica delere moliuntur, a nequissimis eorum propositis et insultibus, quibus in christianum sanguinem et catholicos sacerdotes sepenumero debacantur, non solum spiritualibus, verum eciam temporalibus conuocatis præsidiis possimus auctore domino cohercere.
units.en: Considering therefore that the nurslings of iniquity, the Wyclifites and Hussites and other heretics and unbelievers, who, leaving the path of true salvation, make themselves the fiercest persecutors of the Christian religion, and who, striving to overthrow the orthodox faith with false and insane dogmas, condemned errors and the kindling of heresies, have infected the whole kingdom of Bohemia and the lands bordering it; and desiring to oppose their rashness as far as we can with God, we have resolved to rouse the faithful soldiers, champions of Christ, athletes marked with the sign of the life-giving cross by which he redeemed us from damnation, against the said heretics, so that, by the Lord's authority, we may restrain these heretics, who, casting off the fear of God, burn and overthrow churches, monasteries and other holy places dedicated in honour of Christ and of the glorious Virgin, of the apostles, martyrs and confessors, and their images, and who strive to destroy the catholic faith above all in the German nation, from their most wicked designs and assaults, in which they often rage against Christian blood and catholic priests, not only by spiritual but also by temporal forces called together.
units.note: The charge the bull makes is the burning of churches, monasteries and images, and violence against priests: what Laurence of Březová records of the Taborites at Beroun and elsewhere (Laurence Towns [4]). 'Above all in the German nation': the crusade is preached as the defence of Germany.

units.titel: The legate, an angel of peace
units.orig: Hodie siquidem pro succidendis ex agro dominico vepribus pestiferis et nociuis et quibuscunque peruersis erroribus de hereticorum ipsorum mentibus exstirpandis, illorumque salubri reduccione ad gremium sancte matris ecclesie, ut ad cor reuersi ab huiusmodi resipiscant erroribus, quibus gregem ipsum seducere et inficere moliuntur, et si in eorum obstinacione et malignitate permanserint euertantur, te ad regnum præfatum nec non marchionatus Morauie et Misne eorumque prouincias, ciuitates, terras et loca eisdem heresibus et erroribus polluta, tibi plene potestatis legati de latere officium committendo de fratrum nostrorum consilio tamquam pacis angelum præuidimus destinandum, prout in aliis nostris desuper confectis literis plenius continetur.
units.en: For today, to cut out of the Lord's field the pestilent and harmful thorns, and to root out every perverse error from the minds of these heretics and bring them back to the bosom of holy mother church, so that, returning to their hearts, they may recover from the errors with which they strive to seduce and infect the flock, and, if they remain in their obstinacy and malice, may be overthrown, we have, on the advice of our brothers, decided to send you as an angel of peace to the said kingdom and to the margraviates of Moravia and Meissen and their provinces, cities, lands and places polluted by these heresies and errors, committing to you the office of legate a latere with full power, as is more fully contained in our other letters on this matter.
units.note: Branda da Castiglione, cardinal priest of San Clemente, is sent as legate 'a latere', with the pope's full power. 'If they remain in their obstinacy, let them be overthrown': conversion first, war after.

units.orig: omnes et singulos reges, duces, marchiones, principes, barones, comites, capitaneos, magistratus et quoslibet alios officiales eorumque loca tenentes, communitates quoque et vniuersitates ciuitatum, terrarum et opidorum, castrorum, villarum et aliorum quorumcunque locorum, ceterosque christiani nominis zelatores status et religionis cuiuslibet, ubilibet dominantes et constitutos rogamus et hortamur, ac per aspersionem sanguinis eiusdem gloriosissimi redemptoris paternis affectibus obsecramus, in suorum remissionem peccaminum suadentes, ut ad Hussitarum, Wicleuistarum et aliorum hereticorum præfatorum subuersionem et exterminium et ad impendenda tibi contra nos profutura suffragia, quibus huiusmodi negocii prosecucio feliciter adiuuetur, potenter atque viriliter se accingant, quos spiritualibus donis, indulgenciis videlicet et remissionibus de ipsorum fratrum consilio prouidimus inuitandos.
units.en: We ask and exhort all and each, kings, dukes, margraves, princes, barons, counts, captains, magistrates and any other officials and their lieutenants, the communities and corporations of cities, lands and towns, castles, villages and all other places, and all other zealots of the Christian name of whatever status and religion, wherever they rule or are placed, and we beseech them with a father's love by the sprinkling of the blood of the same most glorious Redeemer, urging it for the remission of their sins, that they gird themselves powerfully and manfully for the overthrow and extermination of the said Hussites, Wyclifites and other heretics, and for giving you the help against them, by which the conduct of this business may be happily furthered; and we have decided, on the advice of the same brothers, to invite them with spiritual gifts, namely indulgences and remissions.
units.note: The crusade is addressed, like the ordinance, to every estate from kings to villages. The ordinance bound the brethren with penalties; the bull draws the crusaders with indulgences. 'Contra nos', against us, is printed so; the sense requires 'contra eos', against them, and so it is translated.

units.titel: Preaching the cross: a hundred days for listening
units.orig: Quocirca circumspeccioni tue per apostolica scripta committimus et mandamus, quatenus tu per te uel venerabiles fratres nostros patriarchas archiepiscopos et episcopos ac dilectos filios electos administratores, abbates, priores, aliosque ecclesiarum et monasteriorum prælatos et ceteros christiane religionis professores ubilibet residentes, quos tibi adiutores super hijs duxeris eligendos, quociens per te uel deputandos a te contra hereticos prælibatos exercitum conuocari uel expedicionem aut quamuis ordinacionem fieri contigerit, ad præmissum tam salubre negocium prosequendum veluti præcones fortes exaltando in ipso crucis nomine voces vestras in singulis ciuitatibus, dyocesibus atque locis, [...] quibuscunque Christi fidelibus ad id audiendum confluentibus, quibus vere penitentibus et confessis, ut ad id libencius inducantur, pro vice qualibet accessus eorum centum dies de iniunctis eis penitenciis [...] relaxentur, verbum crucis eiusdem ac ipsius admirabile signum publice proponere et publicare procures, [...] eorumque humeris affigas et affigant.
units.en: Wherefore we commit and command to your circumspection by apostolic letters that, whenever an army is called or an expedition or any other ordinance is made against the said heretics by you or those you depute, you, by yourself or by our venerable brothers the patriarchs, archbishops and bishops, and our beloved sons the elect, administrators, abbots, priors and other prelates of churches and monasteries and other professors of the Christian religion wherever they reside, whom you choose as your helpers, lifting your voices like strong heralds in the very name of the cross in every city, diocese and place, [...] take care to set forth and proclaim publicly the word of the cross and its wondrous sign to all the faithful of Christ who come together to hear it; to whom, being truly penitent and confessed, a hundred days of the penance enjoined on them shall be remitted for each time they come, so that they may be the more willingly drawn to it; [...] and that you and they fix the cross on their shoulders.
units.note: Even hearing the crusade sermon earns a hundred days' indulgence, each time. The preaching ran through the German dioceses; Andreas of Regensburg, in whose collection the bull survives, copied the documents of this campaign.

units.titel: Plenary remission for those who go
units.orig: eisdem fidelibus, qui crucis eiusdem signo suscepto per et infra illud tempus, quod per te uel alium in huiusmodi prædicacione eis duxeris præfigendum, et quociens pro extirpacione eorundem heresum ad te uel quo fideles ipsos contra eosdem hereticos destinando transmiseris veniendo præfato exercitui in personis propriis interfuerint et expensis, quique ut illis interessent sine fraude iter arripuerint, si in ipso fuerint itinere vita functi, plenam suorum peccaminum, de quibus corde contriti et ore confessi extiterint, veniam impartimur, et in retribucione iustorum salutis eterne policemur augmentum;
units.en: to those faithful who, having taken the sign of the cross, within the time you or another fix for them in such preaching, and as often as, coming to you or wherever you send them against these heretics for the rooting out of these heresies, take part in the said army in their own persons and at their own expense, and to those who set out without fraud to take part and die on the way, we grant full pardon of their sins, of which they are contrite in heart and have confessed with their mouth, and promise them an increase of eternal salvation in the reward of the just;
units.note: The crusader pays for himself and earns the full indulgence: the same principle as the Frankfurt diet's 'everyone at his own cost' (Orders 1427 [2]).

units.titel: Those who pay, those who pray
units.orig: eisque, qui non in personis propriis illuc accesserint, sed ipsorum dumtaxat expensis iuxta suarum facultatum qualitatem et exigenciam ydoneos destinauerint bellatores, ac illis, qui licet alienis expensis, propriis tamen adierint in personis, plenam suorum concedimus veniam peccatorum. Ceteris vero qui in personis propriis interesse et propter inopiam suis expensis alios destinare nequiuerint, dummodo huiusmodi durante persecucione negocii in jeiuniis et oracionibus perseuerent, suppliciter exorando, quod altissimus dignetur ipsis fidelibus contra ipsos hereticos victoriam elargiri, sexaginta dies de iniunctis eis penitenciis misericorditer relaxamus; huiusmodi quoque remissionis volumus et concedimus esse participes iuxta quantitatem subsidii et deuocionis affectum eos omnes, qui durantibus expedicione et exercitu supradictis pro huiusmodi consumacione negocii congrue ministrauerint, et circa illud consilium et auxilium impenderint oportuna.
units.en: and to those who do not go there in person but, at their own expense alone, according to the kind and measure of their means, send suitable fighters, and to those who go in person though at another's expense, we grant full pardon of their sins. But to the others, who cannot take part in person and because of poverty cannot send others at their own expense, provided they persevere in fasting and prayer while this business is pursued, humbly praying that the Most High deign to grant the faithful victory over these heretics, we mercifully remit sixty days of the penance enjoined on them; and we will and grant that all those who, while the said expedition and army last, minister fittingly to the completion of this business and give fitting counsel and help, share in this remission according to the amount of their contribution and the warmth of their devotion.
units.note: A scale of grace by means: full remission for those who fight or pay a fighter, sixty days for the poor who fast and pray, and a share 'according to the amount of the contribution' for those who give. The ordinance divided booty 'among the rich and the poor as is befitting' (Ordinance [7]); the bull divides grace by what each can pay.

units.titel: Absolution even for arson and sacrilege
units.orig: Vniuersis præterea et singulis, quos eodem signo crucis muniri contigerit, ut præfertur, illo priuilegio illaque immunitate gaudere decernimus, que cruce signatis pro terre sancte subsidio in generali concilio sunt concessa, eorumque personas nec non familiam, res et bona sub beati Petri et dicte sedis atque nostra proteccione permanere debere, [...] tibi et eisdem patriarchis, archiepiscopis et electis, abbatibus et prælatis, [...] ut omnium pro huiusmodi expedicione negocii crucesignatorum confiteri volencium confessiones audire, ac ipsis confessionibus diligenter auditis pro peccatis suis ac excessibus omnibus per illos commissis, eciam si manuum in clericos et religiosos aut incendiarii et sacrilegi fuerint, debite absolucionis beneficium impendere et iniungere penitenciam salutarem; eciamsi huiusmodi peccata tam grandia et enormia essent, propter que sedes apostolica foret merito consulenda, libere et licite valeatis auctoritate apostolica tenore præsencium indulgemus.
units.en: Moreover we decree that each and all who are marked with the sign of the cross, as said above, shall enjoy the privilege and immunity granted in the general council to those signed with the cross for the aid of the Holy Land, and that their persons, households, goods and property shall remain under the protection of blessed Peter, of the said see and of ourselves, [...] and we grant by the tenor of these presents that you and the said patriarchs, archbishops and elect, abbots and prelates [...] may freely and lawfully, by apostolic authority, hear the confessions of all crusaders of this expedition who wish to confess, and, having diligently heard them, give them the benefit of due absolution for all their sins and excesses and enjoin a salutary penance, even if they have laid violent hands on clerics and religious, or have been arsonists and committers of sacrilege, even if these sins are so great and enormous that the apostolic see would rightly have to be consulted.
units.note: The bull condemns the Hussites for burning churches and attacking priests (Bull [1]) and empowers the legate's confessors to absolve crusaders who have done the same. The Hussite crusade receives the privileges of the crusade to the Holy Land.
